To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effect of reflective/abstrative text on learning is moderated by the cohesiveness level of that text, and by the level of the student's prior knowledge, and that the effect of cohesiveness on learning depends upon the level of the students' prior knowledge.

(i) the level of cohesion in a reflective/abstraction text can be adjusted according to students' prior knowledge to improve the learning gains of middle motivation students; and (ii) high knowledge students learn significantly more from high cohesion than low cohesion reflective/abstraction texts.

(a) providing a reflective/ abstractive post-tutoring text can significantly improve what students learn from a qualitative physics tutoring session, and (b) the effect can be improved by adjusting the cohesion of that text according the students' level of knowledge, but that the effect is not the same for high and low knowledge students.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the interaction between knowledge and text cohesiveness in learning from reflective text.
the effects of knowledge and cohesion on learning in the post-tutoring period.
the question of how to best provide a reflective/abstactive text to help students learn from tutoring.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of the text is dependent on the student's prior knowledge and that this effect is mediated by the cohesiveness (and other features) of the text.
the more knowledge students have, the more they benefit from a high cohesion text.
the more knowledge the student has, the more they learn from a high cohesion reflective text.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
students' learning is significantly improved if the cohesiveness level of the post-tutoring text is adjusted according to their prior knowledge.
the effect of cohesiveness is not uniform across all levels of knowledge.
providing a reflective text can improve learning from tutoring and that adjusting the cohesiness of that text according its students' level of knowledge can improve learning even more.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the context of post-tutoring reflective text, the level of prior knowledge and text cohesiveness interact to influence the learning outcomes.
it is important to consider both the knowledge and motivational aspects of students when designing learning environments, and that the two can interact in non-intuitive ways.
it is important to take into account both students' prior knowledge and the nature of their learning interactions with a tutor when designing a post-tutoring intervention.
